title: You can’t comb a hairy ball flat without leaving a cowlick
body: The hairy ball theorem, first proved by Henri Poincaré in 1885 for the ordinary sphere, says that any continuous pattern of arrows lying flat along a sphere’s surface must have at least one point where the arrow shrinks to zero. Comb a fuzzy ball and you’ll always leave a tuft or a bald spot. Applied to an idealised Earth, it means that on any shell of the atmosphere there is always somewhere with no horizontal wind. A doughnut, by contrast, can be combed perfectly flat.

slides.question: Which of these surfaces can be combed perfectly flat?
slides.explanation: A doughnut can be combed flat, but any continuous combing of a sphere leaves at least one point where the arrow shrinks to zero: a tuft or a bald spot. Poincaré proved it in 1885.
